1 طَنِىَ , aor.
طَنَىَ , (S, K,) inf. n. طَنًى, (S,) said of a camel, He had his spleen adhering to his side in consequence of vehement thirst: (S:) or, said of a man, he had his spleen and his lungs adhering to the ribs on the left side, (K, TA,) so that, sometimes, they become putrid and black; but mostly this is the case in camels; (TA;) as also ↓ اطنى : (K:) or he (a man) had a tertian fever, and his spleen in consequence became enlarged: (Lh, * TA:) and, said of a camel, his spleen became enlarged in consequence of the [disease of the lungs called] نُحَاز. (Lh, TA.) [And طَنِئَ is a dial. var. thereof.] ―
-b2- And, said of a man, i. q. ضَنِىَ [i. e. He was, or became, slender, and small in body: or diseased, disordered, or sick: or lean, or emaciated: &c.]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
